rules.label: Free care at or below 100% FPL
rules.quote: Patients whose family income is at or below 100% of the FPL are eligible to receive free care.

rules.label: Up to 50% discount between 100% and 150% FPL
rules.quote: Patient whose family income is over 100% and below 150% of the FPL would be eligible for up to a 50% discount.

rules.quote: Patients whose family income exceeds 150% of the FPL may be eligible to receive discounted rates on a case-by-case basis based on their specific circumstances, such as catastrophic illness or medical indigence, at the discretion of Community Hospital

notes: Policy reserves right to exclude or limit non-urgent services from FAP
Financial assistance is last resort after exploring all other payment options (private insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, CHP, liability, Crime Victims, CICP)
Elective procedures and flat rate procedures including cosmetic, bariatric lithotripsy are not eligible; complications from elective procedures considered case-by-case
Duration of eligibility does not exceed 12 months; hospital may reevaluate if income changes or new hospital care needed
Relatives/guardians may apply for incapacitated or deceased individuals
Income determination uses gross personal and business income per CICP guidelines; includes all household members and legally responsible parties
AGB (Amounts Generally Billed) calculated per IRC 501(r) rules; recalculated annually May 1-April 30
Patient must submit documentation: minimum last year's tax return, last 3 months income, or bank statement with checking/savings/investment balances
Completed applications processed within 30 days; written notification within 30 days of receipt
Applicant denied has right to appeal in writing to Business Office Manager within 30 days of denial receipt
Applicant must provide required information within 14 days of application date; failure may result in denial
Misrepresentation/falsification causes financial assistance to be withdrawn retroactively
Records maintained for at least 7 years
Hospital may use outside agencies to estimate income when documentation lacking
Collections policy: reasonable efforts to determine eligibility before ECA; ECA includes wage garnishments, liens on primary residences, other legal actions
Collection activity suspended during financial assistance review; resumes if partial adjustment, failure to cooperate, or ineligibility
Hospital complies with all federal, state, and local laws
Hospital located at 2351 G Road, Grand Junction, CO 81505

notes: The policy states that financial assistance benefits are provided as a last resort and all other payment options must be explored prior to application.
The policy allows the hospital to exclude or limit non-urgent services from financial assistance.
The policy specifies that elective procedures and flat rate procedures including cosmetic, bariatric lithotripsy are not eligible for charity care.
The policy states that the term of benefits granted will not exceed twelve months and is subject to financial and medical circumstances.
The policy requires applicants to provide required information within 14 days of the application date or risk denial.
The policy allows for reconsideration of a denial within 30 days of receipt of the denial.
The policy states that misrepresentation or falsification of information will cause financial assistance to be withdrawn retroactively and currently.
The policy indicates that records relating to application and determination will be maintained for at least 7 years.
The policy indicates that the hospital will use gross personal and business income consistent with CICP program guidelines for income determination.
The policy states that the hospital will provide an itemized statement showing charges and discount amount applied once a complete application is submitted.
The policy indicates that the hospital will notify the patient or applicant in writing within 30 days of receipt of a completed application.
The policy states that the hospital will not engage in extraordinary collection actions before making a reasonable effort to determine financial assistance eligibility.
The policy defines extraordinary collection actions as wage garnishments, liens on primary residences, or other legal actions.

The policy states that if a collection agency identifies a patient meeting financial assistance eligibility criteria, the account may be considered for financial assistance and collection activity suspended.
The policy indicates that the hospital complies with all other federal, state, and local laws, rules, and regulations.
